reports.title: On April 14, 2026, the Company completed the acquisition of Foran Mining Corporation (“Foran”) (Note 4). The results of operations of Foran are included in these condensed consolidated interim financial statements from April 14, 2026.

guidance.heading: 2026 Outlook
section: Based on year-to-date performance through the third quarter, Eldorado has revised its 2026 production outlook for its operating assets, excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, to 410,000 to 430,000 ounces of gold, compared with original guidance of 430,000 to 490,000 ounces. The revised 2026 production outlook, including Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, is 425,000 to 475,000 ounces of gold, compared with original guidance of 495,000 to 600,000 ounces. Strong performance at Lamaque, supported by increasing contributions from high-grade Ormaque ore, is partially offsetting lower expected production at Kisladag and Olympias as well as the impact of a slower than expected ramp-up at Skouries.

•Lamaque – Strong operating execution and increasing contributions from high-grade Ormaque ore continue to support strong production performance. Ormaque is becoming an increasingly important source of high-grade ore for Lamaque.

•Kisladag – Lower production for 2026 primarily reflects lower-grade ore associated with the current mining sequence and slower than planned mining progress during the third quarter, which delayed access to higher-grade material. Higher-grade material is now being stacked on the North Heap Leach Pad; however, given the approximately 300-day leach cycle, the associated production benefit is expected toward the end of the fourth quarter and into 2027.

•Olympias – Lower production for 2026 primarily reflects the timing of the 650 ktpa expansion, which reduces expected fourth-quarter throughput and production. The targeted 650 ktpa nameplate throughput rate is expected to be achieved in the first half of 2027. In addition, material with elevated lead and zinc content that was expected to be processed during the third quarter was instead stockpiled. This material is expected to be introduced through a controlled blending program during the fourth quarter to maintain stable plant performance and optimize recoveries.

•Skouries – Gold production guidance for 2026 has been revised to 10,000 to 35,000 ounces, compared with prior guidance of 60,000 to 100,000 ounces, reflecting a slower-than-expected ramp-up. The revision reflects the timing of the ramp-up and does not change the Company’s expectations for Skouries’ longer-term design capacity with commercial production expected in late Q4 2026.
•McIlvenna Bay – Gold production continues to track within the 5,000 to 10,000 ounce guidance range for 2026. Commercial production is expected in late Q4 2026.
